name: The Seedways
description: Generations after the Blight Year emptied the fields, valley towns survive on shared seed stock hauled by caravan along the seedway routes between the last granary and the first orchards.

locations.name: Granary Hill
locations.description: Terraced seed-vaults cut into the hill, where the tithe grain is graded and sealed.

locations.name: Ford Market
locations.description: The river-crossing market where the seedways meet and the weigh-house keeps the tithe ledgers.

locations.name: The Ash Orchards
locations.description: Replanting rows on blight-ash soil, tended by families who took the worst land first.

locations.name: The Frost Gate
locations.description: The high pass that closes on the last frost and strands whatever is caught beyond it.

factions.name: The Seed Keepers
factions.description: A caravan order sworn to grade, seal and carry seed stock between the valleys.

factions.name: The Millers' Compact
factions.description: The town millers who weigh tithe grain and hold the market charters.

factions.name: The Orchard Families
factions.description: The planters who took the blight-ash land and are owed grafting stock by the vaults.

rules.statement: Every town that draws from the seed vaults returns two measures at harvest for each measure taken.
No powered machinery survived the Blight; all work is done by hand, beast and water.
The Frost Gate closes on the last frost; a caravan caught beyond it winters alone.
A keeper who adulterates seed stock is struck from the rolls and their name is never carried by the caravans again.

history.name: The Blight Year
history.description: The blight emptied the fields; survivors sealed the first vaults on Granary Hill.

history.name: The First Seedway
history.description: The first caravan circuit joined the three valleys and made the tithe system possible.

history.name: The Millers' Split
history.description: A falsified tithe ledger at Ford Market split the routes for a generation.

conflicts.name: The Cut Grain
conflicts.description: Someone is diluting tithe grain with chaff at the weigh-house, and the keepers and millers each blame the other.

conflicts.name: The Orchard Claims
conflicts.description: The orchard families claim vault grain promised to them is being carried to the caravan instead.
